- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior 7-day high), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; reduce forecast by 1–3% to account for mean reversion.
- If sentiment is neutral or slightly positive (avg > -0.2), model frequently underestimates upward momentum; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for 3–7 day horizon.
- Model tends to lag in early 30-day forecasts when sentiment is volatile; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead if sentiment shows strong upward momentum.
- When sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative values), model underestimates true volatility; increase forecast variance by 0.5–1.0% to reflect higher risk.
- For 30-day horizon, if model forecast is consistently below 65.0, and sentiment is negative, add 1–2% to forecast to avoid “floor bias” in downward trends.
